name: Latvia
summary: Latvian law guarantees close relatives a reserved share, paid in money. A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Latvia has no trusts, and foundations exist, but private-benefit use is not confirmed.
reserved_share: Persons entitled to a reserved share (Civil Law, Art. 423 as amended 2014) can claim its value in money. The page does not give who or what fraction, and it was not found elsewhere.
foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
trust_note: Latvia is not in the HCCH table for the 1985 Trusts Convention. Trusts have not been introduced in Latvian law. Foundations are governed by the Law on Associations and Foundations; no profit may be distributed, and private-benefit use was not confirmed.
open_questions: Beneficiaries and the fraction of the reserved share (Civil Law Art. 423 ff) were not sourced.
Whether Latvian foundations may pursue private-benefit purposes was not confirmed.
Foreign trust tax and recognition treatment not sourced.

sources.title: HCCH status table: Convention of 1 July 1985 on the Law Applicable to Trusts and on their Recognition
